current_date: March 2025 (approved by Planning Committee 5 March 2025, item P/64/24)
current_evidence: Planning Committee on 5 March 2025 (item P/64/24) approved the 'National and Local Validation Requirements List' for publication on the council website. Its 51-item numbering matches the item numbers in Grokbot's extracted text (e.g. 47 Active Travel England toolkit, 51 Nutrient strategy), and searches found no later list.

issues.detail: Grokbot's stockton.gov.uk PDF link returned a client error when fetched, so it may have moved or the site may block automated access. The stockton.gov.uk/planning-process page, recorded as the documentation URL on planning.data.gov.uk, has no link to the checklist. Contents were checked against the committee-approved Appendix 1 on moderngov, which appears to be the same 2025 edition. The reference row's 'Planning page' is only the council homepage.
issues.evidence: WebFetch of workbook URL: 'failed at its site (client_error)'; planning-process page: 'no links ... to a validation checklist'

issues.detail: List date 2025-02-01 comes from PDF metadata (CreationDate). The document is headed March 2025 and was approved by Planning Committee on 5 March 2025.
issues.evidence: 'National and Local Validation Requirements List, Planning Committee, March 2025'; resolution P/64/24 on 5 March 2025

issues.detail: The source has 51 items, 43 of them local, but Grokbot's app_type_rows hold only about 25 requirements. Missing local items: 9 Site/Block Plan with parking (includes householder extensions affecting parking or bedrooms); 15 Statement of Community Involvement (30+ dwellings, 10,000 sq m+ non-residential, or controversial schemes); 18 Housing Statement (major housing, 2+ affordable and market dwellings, PBSA; captured only as a garbled 'Affordable Housing Statement'); 19 Retail or Leisure Impact Assessment; 20 Farm Diversification Plan; 21 Employment Land Statement (loss of B1/B2/B8 land); 23 Travel Plan (all majors); 26 Flood Risk Assessment (FZ2/3/3b, 1 ha+ in FZ1, critical drainage areas); 27 SuDS (10+ dwellings or 0.5 ha+, or 1,000 sq m+ non-residential; appears only under prior approval); 28 Agricultural Land Classification; 30 Landscape Character / LVIA (buildings over 20m, masts over 25m in open countryside, EIA cases); 31 Sustainability Standards / BREEAM (all non-residential); 34 Noise Impact and Vibration Assessment; 36 Connectivity Statement (broadband); 38 Playing Fields / Loss of Sports Facilities Statement; 39 ICNIRP Certificate (telecoms); 40 Heritage Statement incl. archaeology (listed buildings, LBC, conservation area demolition, CA schemes of 1+ dwelling); 44 Lighting Assessment; 45 Sequential Test for main town centre uses (Policy EG3); 46 Design Checklist / Building for a Healthy Life (major housing); 47 Active Travel England Planning Assessment Toolkit (all majors; appears only as a tab_items fragment); 48 Dust Control Assessment (demolition, earthworks, construction, trackout); 50 Hot Food Takeaway Impact Statement (outside defined centres).
issues.evidence: Appendix 1, National and Local Validation Requirements List (March 2025), items 9-51

issues.detail: Householder is marked '(none) - national requirements only', but item 9 explicitly requires parking details for householder extensions that affect parking or add bedrooms. Item 24 (trees on or within 10m of the site) and item 32 (land contamination screening form for small schemes) also reach householder proposals. Listed building consent shows only the DAS, though the Heritage Statement (40) and Structural Survey (42) apply to LBC. Demolition in a conservation area is '(none)', though item 40 covers conservation area demolition. Outline is '(none)', though the many 'all major applications' items apply to outline majors.
issues.evidence: Item 9 Site/Block Plan: '... householder extensions affecting parking or bedrooms'; Item 40: 'conservation area demolition, listed building consent'

issues.detail: Some rows are filed under the wrong application type because of keyword matches. 'Structural Survey' sits under Minerals & waste because its excerpt runs on into item 43; item 42 actually covers conversions, agricultural buildings and listed-building demolition. 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' sits under Change of use - prior approval because the FRA text mentions a 'change of use ... to a more vulnerable class'. Nearly all other rows (about 25, e.g. Air Quality, Tree survey, Archaeology, Nutrient Neutrality, Viability) carry 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', although the list sets triggers by scale, location or use (e.g. all majors, all new residential).
issues.evidence: Item 42 Structural Survey: conversions outside development limits / agricultural buildings / listed building demolition; Item 43: mineral, landfill and landraise applications

issues.detail: Several triggers are taken from the wrong item. Transport Assessment's excerpt is the air-quality sentence ('more than 500AADT car movements ... Air Quality Assessment is required'); the real trigger is majors (TA) and smaller schemes with significant traffic (TS). Planning Statement's excerpt is EIA text ('If the project is listed in Schedule 1...'); the real trigger is all majors and departures. Open space's excerpt is viability text about S106 contributions; the real trigger is development in designated open space and majors. 'Design Code / Masterplan' is really the drainage masterplan sentence from the SuDS item. 'Ground investigation / Geotechnical' is really item 43, Hydrogeological Risk Assessment.
issues.evidence: Item 16 Planning Statement: 'all major applications and any departure from the development plan'; Item 29 Open Space: 'development in designated open space, and major applications'

issues.detail: Many triggers are cut-off fragments that do not say when the item applies: Ecology 'of any protected species.'; HIA 'to submit a Health Impact Assessment.' (real trigger: 100+ dwellings, other majors, and significant health impacts, for applications from 1 Oct 2025); Planning Obligations 'from the S106 agreement.' (real: majors needing S106); Nutrient Neutrality uses explanatory text (real: all new residential development); Air Quality gives only the AADT traffic route and omits 'all major developments'; the AIA excerpt is cut off mid-sentence; Affordable Housing contains reviewer wording ('I would add a requirement for;'); DAS and Parking excerpts are run-together URLs and table headers.
issues.evidence: Item 49 HIA: 'residential schemes of 100+ dwellings, other major non-residential schemes...'; Item 51: 'all new residential development'; Item 35: 'all major developments'

issues.detail: Almost all 16 tab_items are boilerplate or fragments rather than requirements. They include guidance URLs with table headers ('No National Information / Local Item Policy Driver Applications that require this information'), process text ('Planning permission is not considered granted and will not be issued until the S106 Agreement is completed'), an SCI fragment ('how any difficulties were overcome...'), three sentences explaining what nutrient neutrality is, a landscape map sentence filed under SuDS guidance, and a 'Building Regs AD M' URL run into the Retail Impact heading.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' entries; e.g. 'Using nutrient neutrality, developers only pay for mitigation required...'

issues.detail: 'Biodiversity Checklist / Questionnaire' and 'Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) information / metric' are both the same BNG Strategy item (4, all majors excluding exempt development) with identical excerpt text. 'Design and Access Statement' is also repeated under Full and LBC with the same garbled excerpt.
issues.evidence: Item 4 Biodiversity Net Gain Strategy: 'all major applications, excluding exempt development'

summary: Grokbot found the right 2025 edition of Stockton's National and Local Validation Requirements List (approved 5 March 2025), but the URL could not be fetched and the date comes from PDF metadata. The extraction is poor: about 25 of 43 local items are missing, the Householder row wrongly says '(none)', and many triggers are taken from neighbouring items or are cut-off fragments.
